The Digital-Currency Divide

Howard Davies

The rush to develop central bank digital currencies has slowed as underwhelming demand and mounting costs have given governments second thoughts. But while the Federal Reserve and other central banks have shelved their plans, the European Central Bank is pressing ahead with its digital euro.

Pierre Crom/Getty Images

Nov 12, 2026
5 min read

LONDON—Seven years ago, the Group of Thirty’s International Banking Seminar, held alongside the International Monetary Fund’s annual meetings in Washington, featured a presentation by David Marcus, who headed Libra, Facebook’s cryptocurrency project. Marcus tried to persuade the assembled bankers and central bankers that Libra would make banking cheaper and easier, especially for unbanked people in emerging markets.
